compared: after each case's steps: every session as Node's reader reads it from its log (valid, header, messages), whether every legacy json kept its bytes and mtime, and the leftover .tmp files; the disk-full case also after its failed run

differences.legacy jsons after a completed run: Node keeps every legacy json byte for byte (jsonsUnchanged: true); the core removes them once the run is verified complete. Decision: no rollback support (rust-core decisions.md:12, "Version transition"); the core asserts it in native/core/crates/mixdog-migrate/tests/it/recorded_145.rs:149 (`data/sessions/*.json` removed by contract). The replay checks that Node kept them, that the core left none after a complete run, and that a run which did not complete changed none.

excluded.a busy session is skipped and retried at: equality impossible: Node skips a session whose writer claim another process holds (session-log-migration.mjs:250, MIGRATION_SKIP.BUSY :43), migrating after boot beside running writers; the core migrates at boot step 5 under the data dir's lock, before anything serves (native/core/crates/mixdog-app-server-daemon/src/boot.rs:1-7), so no writer can hold a session
excluded.a file that fails verification is skippe: nothing outside the module can reach it: VERIFY_MISMATCH (session-log-migration.mjs:56) needs a loader that reads the same json differently twice; the test injects one (`unstableLoad`, session-log-migration.test.mjs:104); the product's LEGACY_SESSION_LOADER is a pure parse of the bytes, so no product json fails this verification

loader: the product's LEGACY_SESSION_LOADER (the test passes its fixture loader); the claim is the test's held claim

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder
